length.text: About 2 m on average; up to about 4 m

reproduction.text: Lays eggs, 10 to 50 at a time

overview.text: The Carpet Python is a large, non-venomous python of Australia and New Guinea. Its patterned skin looks a little like an old carpet. There are several subspecies, including the Diamond Python of south-eastern Australia.

identification.text: A triangular head with a row of heat-sensing pits along the lips. Colour and pattern vary greatly between areas.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Usually about 2 m long, but up to about 4 m; females are often bigger and heavier than males.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Most of mainland Australia except the dry centre, and southern New Guinea (Indonesia and Papua New Guinea).

habitat.text: A wide range of habitats, from rainforest in north-eastern Queensland to river woodlands and forests elsewhere.

behaviour.text: Can be active by day or night and often climbs trees, but also lives on the ground and basks in open spots.

diet.text: Kills its prey by squeezing (constriction): mainly small mammals, birds and lizards.

reproduction.text: Lays 10 to 50 eggs. The mother coils around them and twitches her muscles to warm them until they hatch.

recognise.text: Big python with a triangular head and pits along the lips.
